name: EuroSAT
description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images for land use and land cover classification, consisting of 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced image patches across 10 classes and covering 13 spectral bands.
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2, 2019.
rai:dataCollection: To construct the dataset, the authors performed two steps: (1) satellite image acquisition by gathering Sentinel-2A satellite images of European cities distributed in over 34 countries, choosing images associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas and selecting images with low cloud level; and (2) dataset creation by creating 27,000 geo-referenced and labeled 64x64 image patches from the obtained satellite images. The images were recorded all over the year to increase variance, and all 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral Sentinel-2A satellite images downloaded via Amazon S3, associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas. The source data are openly and freely accessible Sentinel-2 images from ESA's Copernicus program.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Image patches of size 64x64 pixels were extracted from the satellite images to create 27,000 geo-referenced and labeled samples. Bands with lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation for band evaluation experiments.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Satellite images with low cloud level were selected. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and the ground truth was corrected by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. The dataset did not receive atmospheric correction, so samples with color cast due to atmospheric effects were retained in the dataset.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset consists of labeled and geo-referenced image patches created based on classes chosen from the European Urban Atlas mapping guide. The authors manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by removing mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice. They note that some classes are commonly confused, especially the agricultural land classes and the classes highway and river.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Geographic information in the form of geo-referenced images and distribution over European cities in more than 34 countries.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that the resulting classification system opens a gate towards a number of Earth observation applications, including agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, environmental monitoring, land use and land cover change detection, deforestation detection, and assistance in improving and keeping geographical maps up-to-date.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset distribution is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas. The authors selected images with low cloud level and aimed to cover as many countries as possible and images recorded all over the year to capture high intra-class variance. They also note low positive correlation between some classes, especially the two agricultural classes and the residential and industrial building classes.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. A patch-based classifier trained on 64x64 image patches does not allow finely graduated per-pixel segmentation. The classifier sometimes confuses agricultural land classes as well as highway and river.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is presented as a benchmark and basis for large-scale training of deep neural networks for satellite image classification, specifically land use and land cover classification. The paper uses training-test splits for benchmarking and demonstrates applications in land use and land cover change detection and assistance in keeping geographical maps up-to-date.
